Edition 2 · Call for Applications

Build what's next for Africa's smallholder farmers.

A joint SONGA x Kilikawi Challenge for university student teams. Edition 1 asked you to reimagine the Kilikawi tiller that works the farm. Edition 2 widens the lens to the SONGA trike that moves milk to market — real engineering problems, real field tests, real funding.

One challenge, two platforms.

Kilikawi and SONGA are two halves of the same loop — and Edition 2 is the first time student teams get to work on both at once.

Powers the farm.

One electric power unit driving many interchangeable tools — plowing, milling, shelling, chaff cutting, irrigation — instead of a shed full of single-purpose machines. The Swiss-army knife of small-scale farming.

Moves it to market.

Electric cargo trikes, solar charging stations and collection hubs that get milk from a smallholder's yard to a dairy before it spoils — and into the hands of a driver who's paid by the kilometre.

Edition 2 asks you to make both halves work harder: sharper quality control, smarter cargo, new value chains, and a business model that survives contact with the ground.

The four topics.

Two engineering problems, two business-model problems. Pick one — or make the case for your own angle on it.

Engineering / R&D
01

Dairy Collection Quality Control

Too much time is spent per batch quality check (density + freshness) — especially for small collections of 5L or less. How do you get a reliable reading without slowing the driver down?

Engineering / R&D
02

Cargo Configurations on the Trike

How do you keep the cargo area flexible enough to combine feed, milk and other produce — FMCG, parcels — in a single trip, without redesigning the trike from scratch?

Business Model
03

Value Chains & Trike Utilization (TaaS)

Milk's repeatability and perishability make it a strong base load — but collection is mostly a morning job. What else, or who else, can put the trike's afternoon capacity to work?

Business Model
04

Kilikawi Business Model

Service agent vs. community ownership — which holds up best on the ground, for cost, access and upkeep (battery swapping, maintenance)?

This one is scoped as field-testing, not a final design: SONGA's own team keeps ownership of the business-model decision. What we need from you is real pilot evidence on specific variants, run in parallel across teams.

Who can apply.

University student teams of 3–5, from any university, on any topic. We're not naming schools here — our team reaches out directly — but here's the kind of program that tends to fit each theme best.

Topics 01–02 · Engineering / R&D

What we look for
  • Mechanical or electrical engineering tracks
  • Bonus if paired with an agriculture or agri-tech department
  • Hands-on fabrication & prototyping capability

Topics 03–04 · Business Model

What we look for
  • A genuine rural footprint or focus, not just a campus lab
  • Access to smallholder farmers and farming grounds
  • Willingness to field-test ideas, not just model them

What's provided.

Edition 2 is backed by dedicated mentorship and hands-on support — not just a brief.

Mentor support

Mentors scoped to dairy operations, structuring and presentation skills — compensated at $500 for the full period.

Expert resources

On-demand engineer consultations and overview mentors, available throughout the program.

Prize & stipend

Funding to support MVP development, plus a 3-month intern stipend for winning teams.

Exposure

Industry visibility and media coverage for participating teams.
